task: Photonic simulation of vibronic spectra: bridging chemistry and Gaussian boson sampling
key_results: Linear coupling approximation (coherent state sampling) outperforms GBS for formic acid; identified molecular attributes determining when full GBS is unnecessary; improved GBS-chemistry connection established
comments: Important foundational mapping of chemistry approximations to photonic implementations; limited molecular set tested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: GBS is unnecessary for molecules with weak non-Gaussian vibronic character; linear coupling approximation suffices
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for formic acid: coherent state sampling gives improved similarity to experiment vs. GBS

title: Large-scale quantum reservoir computing using a Gaussian Boson Sampler
task: Large-scale quantum reservoir computing using frequency-multiplexed Gaussian boson sampler (>400 modes)
key_results: Access to mode correlations improves accuracy >20 percentage points vs. mean photon number alone; squeezed light consistently yields highest accuracies; GBS effective quantum reservoir at very large system sizes
comments: First experimental evidence supporting theoretical predictions on correlation advantage in quantum machine learning; computational scaling and noise tolerance not thoroughly characterized.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum correlations in GBS output enhance machine learning accuracy beyond mean photon number
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: correlation-based approach achieves 20+ percentage point accuracy advantage on benchmark tasks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Squeezed light improves GBS-based quantum reservoir computing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: squeezed light consistently produces highest accuracies vs. classical light sources

title: Multiuser entanglement distribution network across cryogenic nodes enabled by integrated photonic chips
task: Multiuser entanglement distribution across cryogenic quantum network nodes via integrated photonics
key_results: Five-user fully-connected network with ten entangled photon pairs; all measured raw visibilities exceed classical limit; silicon integrated photonics + superconducting nanowire detectors enable cryogenic deployment
comments: First demonstration of heterogeneously integrated photonic chips for cryogenic quantum networks; scalability beyond five users and network distance not addressed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integrated photonics enables scalable cryogenic entanglement distribution bridging heterogeneous quantum systems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: five-user network demonstrates all-to-all entanglement with classical-limit-exceeding visibilities

title: An integrated DFT + U and device simulation design of doped CsGeCl3 for high efficiency flexible solar absorbers
task: Design of Mn/Fe-doped CsGeCl₃ perovskite for flexible solar cells
key_results: Fe-doped CsGe₀.₈₇₅Fe₀.₁₂₅Cl₃ achieves optimal bandgap 1.21 eV and PCE 31.6%; improved mechanical ductility confirmed
comments: Strong integration of first-principles DFT+U with device simulation (SCAPS-1D); actual device fabrication absent, relying on simulation only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fe doping creates intermediate band enabling sub-bandgap photon absorption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bandgap narrowed from 3.44 eV to 1.21 eV, PCE increased to 31.6%

title: Structural, electrical and hydrogen sensing properties evaluation of fabricated PdO thin films by thermal oxidation
task: Hydrogen sensing in PdO thin films: phase evolution, electrical, and sensing mechanisms
key_results: Full Pd→PdO conversion above 550°C; bandgap 2.06–2.42 eV; dual sensing mechanisms: reversible p-type at ≤1000 ppm H₂, reduction-driven at 2% H₂; room-temperature detection of 1000 ppm H₂
comments: Comprehensive temperature- and thickness-dependent analysis; mechanistic differentiation of sensing regimes is novel, though thickness-dependence limited to 5–20 nm range.

hypotheses.hypothesis: PdO exhibits distinct sensing mechanisms at low and high H₂ concentrations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: reversible p-type reaction at ≤1000 ppm, reduction-driven PdO→Pd at 2% H₂ with sharp resistance drop

title: Corrugated horn antenna with perforated dielectric lens for radar-based level sensing in high-temperature, high-pressure environments
task: Corrugated horn antenna with perforated dielectric lens for high-temperature/high-pressure radar level sensing
key_results: 29.07 dBi gain (3.26 dB improvement over bare horn); HPBWs 6.9° (E-plane) and 6.7° (H-plane); perforated PTFE lens enables equalization at 60 GHz while allowing pressure/thermal equilibration
comments: Practical industrial design with elegant dual-function lens (phase compensation + pressure relief); thermal stability verified only via simulation.

model_io.model: Corrugated horn antenna + perforated PTFE lens

hypotheses.hypothesis: Perforated dielectric lens provides phase compensation while enabling pressure equalization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 3.26 dB gain improvement; perforations allow airflow without degrading beam pattern

title: Natural dyes of mulberry leaf enriched with carbon dots as greener methodology to improve the optical properties of chitosan biopolymer
task: Chitosan biopolymer optical enhancement via natural mulberry leaf dye enriched with carbon dots
key_results: Bandgap reduced from 5.45 eV (pristine CS) to 2.1 eV (doped composite); refractive index increased 1.16→1.22; carbon dot quantum yield 1.76% with blue fluorescence (461 nm); Wemple-DiDomenico model correlates microscopic (charge carrier mobility) with macroscopic (phase velocity) optical properties
comments: Comprehensive green synthesis approach; practical optoelectronic device performance (photocurrent, efficiency) not demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Natural CQD doping significantly reduces bandgap and enhances optical properties of chitosan
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bandgap drops from 5.45 to 2.1 eV; refractive index and dielectric constant enhanced

title: Effect of vanadium layer thickness on the phase transition of fabricated vanadium dioxide thin films
task: Phase transition characterization of VO₂ thin films as function of precursor layer thickness
key_results: Transition temperature and hysteresis strongly depend on vanadium layer thickness (25–90 nm); XRD, Raman, and FTIR used to track phase composition and phase fractions
comments: Systematic thickness-dependent study; mechanistic understanding of oxidation kinetics and O₂ diffusion remains incomplete.

model_io.model: Thermal oxidation of V thin films

hypotheses.hypothesis: Precursor V layer thickness affects oxidation kinetics and final VO₂ properties
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: thickness variation influences phase composition, crystallite size, and transition characteristics

title: Unveiling the electronic and thermodynamic properties of 2-furaldehyde semicarbazone derivatives: combined DFT and M-polynomial topological indices analysis
task: Electronic and thermodynamic properties of 2-furaldehyde semicarbazone derivatives via DFT and topological indices
key_results: E isomer more stable than Z isomer (except FSC: Z +1.1 kcal/mol); rotation barriers 45–97 kcal/mol; E isomer HOMO-LUMO gap lower, higher reactivity; M-polynomial topology correlates with stability and Gibbs energy
comments: Comprehensive multi-method analysis (DFT, QTAIM, NCI, M-polynomial); topological index framework novel but requires experimental validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: E isomer exhibits superior thermodynamic stability and lower kinetic barriers than Z isomer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for derivatives (not FSC): E > Z with lower HOMO-LUMO gap and barriers 45–94 kcal/mol

hypotheses.hypothesis: M-polynomial-derived indices predict chemical reactivity and Gibbs energy trends
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: higher topological indices correlate with lower Gibbs energy and greater stability

title: Uncertainty aware machine learning for bridging simulation and experiment in high throughput materials characterization
task: Uncertainty-aware domain adaptation for bridging simulation-experiment gap in materials characterization
key_results: USEM framework reduces simulation-experiment distribution shift; spectral-normalized neural Gaussian processes enable OOD sample detection; improved XRD peak analysis accuracy on sparse experimental data
comments: Novel integration of adversarial domain adaptation with Bayesian uncertainty; validation limited to XRD, scalability to other modalities unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Domain adaptation in latent space combined with Bayesian uncertainty improves transfer learning for experimental data
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: USEM achieves higher accuracy and OOD robustness than standard ML baseline

title: Acoustic-driven self-rotating cylinders
task: Acoustic radiation-driven self-rotation of cylindrical bodies via metasurface velocity patterns
key_results: Zero net force with non-zero torque achievable via tailored surface velocity distributions; rotation velocity scales predictably with design parameters under low Reynolds number conditions
comments: Elegant analytical framework; experimental validation absent, practical applications to acoustic manipulation speculative.

inputs: imposed normal velocity pattern (amplitude, frequency, phase)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Asymmetric surface velocity distribution generates non-zero net torque while maintaining zero net force
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: designed velocity distributions produce self-rotation; feasibility demonstrated numerically

title: Dual functional device featuring absorption and polarization conversion based on temperature controlled metasurface for terahertz applications
task: Switchable terahertz metasurface with VO₂ for absorption/polarization conversion
key_results: Linear-to-linear cross-polarization converter (88% fractional bandwidth 0.66–1.7 THz) at 298 K; absorber (80%+ absorptivity, 140% bandwidth 0.34–1.96 THz) above 351 K via metal-insulator transition
comments: Simple single-layer design with excellent bandwidth; thermal tuning limits dynamic reconfigurability compared to electrical modulation.

model_io.model: Terahertz metasurface with VO₂ and metallic rings

hypotheses.hypothesis: VO₂ metal-insulator transition enables functional switching between polarization conversion and absorption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 88% FBW LTLPC below 68°C; 140% FBW absorber above 68°C

title: Quantitative predictions of alpha-charmonium correlation functions in high-energy collisions
task: Alpha-charmonium bound states and correlation functions from first-principles interactions
key_results: α-J/ψ system is loosely bound with 0.1–0.6 MeV binding energy; α-ηc exhibits no bound state; source-size-dependent correlation function differences emerge around 3 fm
comments: Rigorous HAL QCD-based potential framework; limited by computational cost to specific spin states.

model_io.model: HAL QCD single-folding potential for α-cc̄

hypotheses.hypothesis: α-J/ψ system exhibits loose binding via long-range attractive interaction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with 0.1–0.6 MeV binding energy; spin-dependent variations measurable

hypotheses.hypothesis: Alpha density distribution affects correlation function shape
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CD vs SG models produce markedly different correlation behaviors despite identical rms radius

title: Reliable equalization aided long-distance OFDM-FSO performance analysis over Gamma–Gamma turbulence with thermal and background noise mitigation
task: FSO-OFDM long-distance inter-satellite communication under turbulence
key_results: BPSK achieves BER 10⁻¹² at 22 dB SNR (weak) and 27 dB (strong turbulence) up to 7000 m; 256-QAM reaches 31.6% efficiency at 11000 m
comments: Practical demonstration of zero-forcing equalization for LEO/MEO links, though comparison with adaptive equalization methods would strengthen claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lower-order modulation (BPSK/QPSK) sustains reliable performance over longer distances in strong turbulence
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: BPSK optimal up to 7000 m; 256-QAM preferred only for 11000 m weak turbulence

title: Velocity-dependent shear band formation in blanking processes
task: Adiabatic shear band (ASB) formation in high-speed blanking of press-hardened steel
key_results: Blanking speed (0.12–17 m/s) significantly influences ASB length, width, and microstructure; 17 m/s achieves full-thickness ASB covering blanked surface; high-speed blanking reduces surface roughness vs. conventional processing
comments: First systematic velocity-dependent ASB study for identical stress state; microstructural strengthening mechanisms of ASBs merit deeper analysis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher blanking velocity promotes full-thickness ASB formation and improved surface quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 17 m/s generates complete ASB spanning sheet thickness with lower roughness

title: Gallium nanostructure fabrication by irradiation with femtosecond laser
task: Hierarchical multiscale LIPSS formation on gallium via femtosecond laser irradiation
key_results: Four hierarchical periodicities: ~10 μm, ~1 μm, ~250 nm, ~30 nm; plasmon-mediated feedback mechanism drives multi-scale self-organization; SPP coupling with localized modes enhances EM confinement
comments: Innovative plasmonic mechanism explanation for subwavelength/deep-subwavelength structures; limited characterization of microstructural properties post-irradiation.

model_io.model: Femtosecond laser interaction with Ga surface

hypotheses.hypothesis: SPP-mediated plasmonic feedback couples wavelength-scale ripples with subwavelength/deep-subwavelength features
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: multiperiodicity coexistence and angular relationships consistent with SPP + localized plasmon coupling

title: Modeling head- and pinna-related transfer functions using boundary elements and finite differences with volume penalization
task: Wave-based HRTF simulation: finite-difference time-domain vs. fast multipole boundary element methods
key_results: FDTD with volume penalization and fmBEM both achieve good agreement with analytical solutions (spherical diffraction) and measured outer ear data; grid requirements for rigid boundaries characterized; FDTD superior for interior problems, fmBEM for exterior domains
comments: Practical comparison supporting HRTF simulation via computationally efficient numerics; perceptual validation against JND thresholds mentioned but not quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FDTD and fmBEM achieve comparable HRTF accuracy within order of magnitude of just-noticeable differences
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: both methods show good agreement with measurements; method choice depends on domain (interior vs exterior)
